title: Sheinbaum Distances Government from CNDH Recommendation, Orders Segob Review
detail: President Claudia Sheinbaum stated 'we did not participate in any way' in the drafting or publication of the CNDH's Recommendation 208VG/2026, saying the Federal Executive was not informed in advance of its release. She ordered the Interior Ministry (Segob) to conduct an exhaustive review of the CNDH report and said her government would present its own investigative advances 'in coming days.' Families' lawyers rejected the CNDH's account, noting the commission did not consult them before publishing the recommendation.

media.caption: President Sheinbaum distances her government from the CNDH's Ayotzinapa recommendation

title: Encinas Releases SEDENA Documents Showing Disappeared Student Was Military Intelligence Asset
detail: Alejandro Encinas, former head of the Ayotzinapa Truth Commission and now Mexico's ambassador to the OAS, publicly released Defense Ministry documents showing that Julio César López Patolzin — one of the 43 disappeared students — had been assigned since June 2014 as a military intelligence asset ('Órgano de Búsqueda de Información') embedded within the Ayotzinapa Rural Normal School, with activity reports dated September 26, 2014 and communications with superior officers. The revelation directly contradicts the CNDH's July 9 recommendation, which dismissed infiltration claims by asserting military personnel could lawfully enroll as students. Families' lawyers and rights organizations cited the documents as further evidence of undisclosed military knowledge of the events.

media.caption: Encinas presents SEDENA documents on student Julio César López Patolzin's alleged military intelligence role

title: Amnesty International: CNDH Recommendation 'Backs State Actions,' Weakens Rights Protections
detail: Amnesty International warned that the CNDH's Recommendation 208VG/2026 'opted to back the actions of the State' and delegitimized the work of international bodies and civil society organizations that have accompanied the families' search for justice. The organization noted that despite 17 Army members linked to legal proceedings in the case, the CNDH exonerated the Defense Ministry citing insufficient evidence, and said the recommendation sends an 'alarming message' about Mexico's institutional commitment to accountability for forced disappearances.

media.caption: Amnesty International criticizes the CNDH's Ayotzinapa recommendation
